coverage: CURRENT-CHANGES.diff: read all six changed Find My paths (onboarding.py, cloudkit/pcs.py, findmy_flow.py, findmy_recovery_guard.py, findmy_setup.py, findmy_vault.py).

custom_components/homecircle/findmy_recovery_guard.py: read in full. Covered the v1->v2 ledger schema, per-account generation, cache witness read/write (no-follow descriptor walk, private-mode checks, size bounds, duplicate-key rejection), the trust gate before begin/reserve/outcome, reset semantics, crash-pending reclassification, counter saturation, unwinding suppression of RecoveryGuardReviewRequired, and hass wiring of the .storage ledger and .cache witness roots.

custom_components/homecircle/findmy_flow.py lines ~215-710: saved-items and add/reconnect vault loading; _findmy_work/_ends_signin terminal routing, including the code-step-only consumed-code set; passcode-step guard status gating; recovery_review/reset acknowledgement (strict `is True`, no automatic proof resubmission, returns to the passcode form); recovery_resume.

custom_components/homecircle/findmy_setup.py: recovery_error mapping (ReviewRequired before Blocked, 429 -> rate_limited); verify_code recovery-stage mapping; check_zone_access/open_recovery diagnostics (fixed allowlists only); _unlock account binding and attempt scoping; discover outcome/resume classification; _outer_auth_failure_reason and _discovery_failure_site, which emit only fixed enums, function names and line numbers.

custom_components/homecircle/_findmy_runtime/onboarding.py: read in full. Covered the RecoveryPETError bounds (status range, phase enum, finite bounded retry_after with ceil), adsid/account-name binding of the fresh PET, PET length bound, and cleanup in finally preserving the primary error.

custom_components/homecircle/_vendor_findmy/cloudkit/pcs.py lines ~780-1040: _signature_key_id_matches is used only as a candidate filter, and verification is always performed under the locally derived or matched key, so accepting a 32-byte P-256 bare x does not weaken authentication. Also covered the outer-signature reason code attachment, require_signature/require_hmac behaviour, the full-length HMAC requirement and the truncated key-id check.

custom_components/homecircle/_vendor_findmy/keychain/escrow.py lines ~140-180 and ~685-800: recovery_attempt fail-closed borrowing; all header/PET preparation finishes before before_dispatch; no auto-retry or redirect on recover; refusal-only `refused()` accounting; uncertain classification of transport and parse failures.

custom_components/homecircle/_vendor_findmy/keychain/recovery.py lines ~380-516: pre-proof not_dispatched paths; guard exceptions from before_dispatch propagate unwrapped, so they map to review/limit/storage codes; verified() runs only after an authenticated SRP server proof; later material failures are classified as 'verified'.

custom_components/homecircle/findmy_vault.py: read in full. The new OSError and invalid-key wrapping into VaultError never replaces key or data. Callers in findmy_flow catch broadly and abort or surface storage errors, so the exception-type change does not alter selection continuity.
docs/RELEASE-1.0-ROLLBACK-PROTECTION.json: read as historical source material only, for the claimed witness root and the claimed ordinary-archive exclusion of the cache witness.

tests: grep-level inventory only (test names and counts in test_findmy_recovery_guard.py, plus targeted grep across tests/ for the changed symbols). Bodies were not read beyond test names. Fresh-account review, ordinary-restore per-account review, ABA rollback, legacy-ledger reset isolation, witness commit failure, unsafe witness, cross-identity witness, and witness outside the ledger tree all appear covered by name. These remain local controls, not independent real-format evidence.

Limitations: bounded ~10-minute review. Not reviewed in depth: cloudkit/beacons.py, cloudkit/records.py, keychain/bottle.py, cuttlefish.py, peers.py, servicekey.py, shares.py, session.py, util/srp.py, der.py, the rest of pcs.py (_find_our_key, meta parsing, DER bounds), findmy_provider.py, findmy_migration.py, findmy_identity.py, findmy_resume.py, the worker/emulator, and the frontend. No code was executed, and no provider, Apple-produced or live interoperability vectors were available.
unresolved_questions: pcs._signature_key_id_matches now also accepts a 32-byte P-256 bare-x key id. That is safe as a filter, because verification still uses the held key and a bare x only names a point up to sign. But I saw no producer-generated vector here showing that Apple emits bare-x signature key ids in inner or outer ObjectSignature candidates. Treat this as a protocol assumption, not a verified format fact.

Rollback protection relies on ordinary HA/Supervisor backups excluding config/.cache. The repo records one scoped native observation that the archive excluded the witness. Whether future Core or Supervisor exclusion lists, or third-party backup add-ons, keep excluding .cache is outside this source's control. If .cache were included, an ordinary restore would bring back a matching ledger/witness pair, which is the same class as the disclosed full-snapshot limit.

The witness digest binds only the per-account entry, including a random generation, not the whole ledger. This looks deliberate (per-account review isolation is tested). A rollback that restores a ledger file byte-identical to the current state for that account is undetectable by design but also harmless.

If attempt.verified() fails on a storage/witness write after an authenticated server proof, the attempt is recorded as 'uncertain' on unwind and discover maps the error to storage or review rather than resume. Recovered in-memory material is then dropped, and a later attempt needs a new proof. This is conservative, not unsafe. Whether it is the intended UX was not confirmed against tests.

_outer_auth_failure_reason only reports when the exception reaching discover is exactly PCSError. If beacons.py or records.py re-wrap PCSError, the diagnostic reason is lost (diagnostic fidelity only). I did not trace the beacon/record wrapping paths.

fresh_recovery_pet and RecoveryGuard.attempt rely on sys.exception() inside a finally block returning the in-flight exception (CPython 3.11+ behaviour). I believe this holds on the recorded 3.14 runtime, but I did not run code to confirm it.
verdict: No confirmed actionable defects in the reviewed scope. The six changed paths and their call chains behave consistently. Guard trust is checked before begin, reserve and every outcome. Missing, mismatched, legacy or unsafe witnesses fail closed to explicit per-account review without auto-repair or proof resubmission. Reservation stays strictly after all credential and header preparation and before transport. Consumed-code recovery errors now end the sign-in instead of re-prompting for a used code. New diagnostics stay within fixed allowlists, and the vault changes never replace stored material. Coverage is partial: several vendor crypto and record modules were not reviewed in depth, and protocol-format assumptions such as bare-x key ids remain unverified without producer vectors. The disclosed full-snapshot joint ledger/witness rollback limit is acknowledged and not counted as a new defect.
